evidence.title: AtaiBeckley Announces Positive Topline Results from an Exploratory Phase 2a Trial of EMP-01 (oral R-MDMA) in Social Anxiety Disorder
Exploratory Safety and Efficacy of EMP-01 in Social Anxiety Disorder (NCT06693609)
AtaiBeckley Announces Positive Topline Results from an Exploratory Phase 2a Trial of EMP-01 (oral R-MDMA) in Social Anxiety Disorder

outcomes.note: The sponsor's topline release of 2026-02-26 reports the primary endpoint (safety and tolerability through Day 43) as met and gives efficacy results: placebo-adjusted LSAS reduction of 11.85 points at Day 43 (Hedges' g 0.45, p=0.036 one-tailed) and CGI-I responders 49% vs 15%; 71 enrolled, 70 dosed, two 225 mg doses 28 days apart, seven UK sites. The trial is the Phase 2 (sponsor label Phase 2a) exploratory randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study NCT06693609 (sponsor atai Therapeutics; ClinicalTrials.gov phase PHASE2; completed 2025-12-10; no results posted there yet). Direction stored as positive as reported by the sponsor; direction is not required. AtaiBeckley was acquired by Eli Lilly on 2026-09-11, after the event.

outcomes.note: The named series is a calendar-year 2026 total, so the proposition cannot become true before the period ends on 2026-12-31 and the source publishes its 2026 figure; as of 2026-09-13 no calendar-2026 figure exists. The packet names the source only as the publisher the forecaster's post cites for a 2025 baseline above US$300M for AI-enabled BCI and neuromodulation health-tech companies; I could not identify that publisher from public pages, so realized_value stays null. Trackers checked, with different company definitions: New Market Pitch (pure-play BCI equity rounds) gives about US$1.0B for 2025 and about US$933M for 2026 through July; Neurofounders gives US$1.75B over the 12 months to March 2026 for 17 BCI companies. Re-resolve after the named source publishes a 2026 total; unresolvable only if none appears within 12 months after the deadline.

ClinicalTrials.gov API record NCT04593875 (results first posted 2026-02-04; intervention other name BX Pulsar 1002)
Dose-Escalation Study of Amygdalar Transcranial Focused Ultrasound in Healthy Volunteers (Neuromodulation)
News - Brain Sonix Corporation

outcomes.note: ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT04593875 (UCLA, PI Bookheimer) were first posted 2026-02-04: a randomized triple-blind sham-controlled crossover trial in 31 Parkinson's patients using the Brainsonix BX Pulsar 1002 (the intervention's listed other name), reporting the primary outcomes (UPDRS-III, finger tapping, 9-hole pegboard) for active vs sham with no meaningful separation; direction is not required. This is an investigator results posting of primary-outcome data in patients dated after 2026-01-01; PubMed shows no earlier publication. Not qualifying: the UT Austin amygdala trial (Mol Psychiatry, epub 2025-04-24), the healthy-volunteer dose-escalation paper (Neuromodulation 2026-04-13) and the medRxiv preprint on thalamic sonication in disorders of consciousness (2026-05-28). Brainsonix issued no topline release in 2026.

evidence.publisher: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin (via CourtListener RECAP)

outcomes.note: Applied as written. H.N. v. Anthem BCBS, Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc. and the Marsh McLennan Plan (D. Mass. 1:26-cv-11454, complaint docketed 2026-03-26) is brought by a plan beneficiary against the claims administrator and the employer that self-funds the plan. Its Second Cause of Action, 'Violation of MHPAEA (Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Claim for Appropriate Equitable Relief under 29 U.S.C. 1132(a)(3)) (ALL DEFENDANTS)', pleads fiduciary breaches by all defendants based on MHPAEA violations in the plan's administration of mental health benefits, so (a) and (b) are met; it is not a suit only under 502(a)(1)(B) against an insurer. Caveats: in substance a benefit-denial suit, not the Schlichter-style class action in the readings; RECAP coverage is partial; a like pleading predates 2026 (W v. Ascension Wisconsin, 2025-09-17). Later alternate: L.P. v. NC Dental Society (2026-04-13).

outcomes.note: Drugs@FDA data (openFDA, updated 2026-09-11) lists 11 ketamine hydrochloride applications, none held by NRx Pharmaceuticals; no KETAFREE or NRX-100 approval exists. NRx's KETAFREE ANDA (received Dec 2025, goal date 2026-07-29) completed first-cycle review on 2026-07-30 with a container-closure deficiency and remained pending after an August 2026 clarification meeting. An ANDA approval would in any case carry only the reference anesthetic indication, not a depressive-disorder indication, and would not count. The NRX-100 NDA for suicidal depression was 'expected to be filed in Q2 2026' (May 2026 release) and the Q2 2026 10-Q still describes cash to 'finance submission' of the NDAs, so no NDA approval is possible as of 2026-09-13.
